sites.functional_impact_measured: Western blot detection of endogenous HA-tagged NRXN3β in neocortical, hippocampal, and cerebellar tissue confirmed successful expression of the tagged full-length protein; no functional assay of synaptic activity or ligand binding reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: The paper explicitly places a double HA tag inside exon 24 of Nrxn3, which encodes the alternatively spliced segment AS5 in the extracellular domain of both alpha and beta isoforms. AS5 is a well-established extracellular insertion point in neurexins. No specific residue number is given in the ledger, so the site is reported at region level with insert_after_residue left null. The knockin strategy in full-length, membrane-anchored protein in vivo is strong evidence that the extracellular loop tolerates the insertion. Knockin mice were generated with a double HA epitope inserted into the coding sequence of Nrxn3 exon 24, which lies within alternatively spliced segment AS5. Both NRXN3α and NRXN3β isoforms carry the tag in the full-length, membrane-anchored context.

sources.claim: We generated knockin mice where a double HA epitope was inserted into the coding sequence of Nrxn3 exon 24 ( Figures 1 B and S1 B).

sites.functional_impact_measured: NOT MEASURED — the ledger clip reports only that the construct was generated; no expression, trafficking, or functional assay result is described.
sites.rationale: The construct name 'V5-Nrxn3' unambiguously places the V5 tag N-terminal to the protein. For a type I TM protein with a signal peptide ending at residue 35, the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 36; a tag upstream of residue 36 would be cleaved with the signal peptide, so the junction is computed as insert_after_residue=35 (residue_before=S, residue_after=S). Python confirmed res(35)='S' and res(36)='S'. No functional data are available from this clip. A V5-tagged full-length Nrxn3 construct ('V5-Nrxn3') was generated for a published study. The naming convention V5-[protein] denotes an N-terminal tag. NRXN3-beta is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein; its only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 35), so the V5 tag must reside there.

literature_notes: L2 is the same knockin experiment as L1 (same paper, same mice, same construct); it was used to confirm the validation_level (detected_only by western blot) but L1 is the primary supporting clip. The V5-Nrxn3 site (L3) is ranked lower because the clip provides no expression or functional readout — only that the construct was made. The AS5 site (L1) is ranked higher because endogenous knockin expression was confirmed by western blot in multiple brain regions, but it remains detected_only because no synaptic or ligand-binding functional assay was reported in the cited clips. No ledger line supports a C-terminal extracellular tag (the C-terminus of NRXN3-beta is intracellular). No ledger line names a specific residue number for either site, so no site reaches 'validated' position_evidence.
